esponses carry that window) subscription rate-limit windows, as read from the anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* response headers. utilization is the fraction of the

rity episodes past the 5-hour limit); resetsAt is unix epoch seconds. Unlike the top-level status/utilization fields, which describe the currently limiting wind
ow, both windows are tracked on every observation, and events are emitted when a window's rounded percentage or reset time moves, not only on status transitions
. Windows absent from the account state are absent here. Absent until the first response carrying these headers is observed, and always absent for API-key, Bedr
ock, and Vertex sessions, whose responses do not carry them.

## usage_limit_reached api_error kind doc
usage_limit_reached: the request was refused by the account's own usage limit, a plan limit (session, weekly or per-model) or a spend cap on usage credits; api_
error_params.rate_limit_info says which and when it resets. The other refusals that share error rate_limit never carry it: an organization policy that turned th

## rate_limit_info inside api_error_params doc
rate_limit_info (usage_limit_reached): what the refused request's own response said about the limit, in the shape rate_limit_event carries. It is read from the 
same values as the message text, so its status, limit and reset are the text's: status is rejected and isUsingOverage false, rateLimitType names the limit, rese
tsAt is when it resets, and overageStatus, overageResetsAt, overageDisabledReason and limitScope say whose spend cap it is (the person's own cap arrives as org_
level_disabled_until, as on rate_limit_event); no other member is sent. It is that refusal's record and is never updated, so compare resetsAt with the clock bef
ore calling the limit current."),api_error_code:o().optional().describe("@internal The server's error.details.error_code for this API error, copied through when

## server contract note (gateway docs): client composes the limit line
Leave \`representative-claim\` and \`overage-status\` off the 429. With them the⏎client composes its own "You've hit your limit" line and drops your message;⏎wi
thout them it prints \`error.message\` as-is (older clients too, behind a⏎generic "API Error" prefix), so put the period, the reset time, and what the⏎user shou
ld do next in that one sentence. \`retry-after\` is seconds until the⏎reset; \`x-should-retry: false\` keeps the SDK from retrying into the block. If⏎you can't 
read your counter and choose to fail closed, send the 429 with⏎\`x-should-retry: false\`,⏎\`anthropic-ratelimit-unified-
